supplemental_sections.review: Introductory heading with a warning that the general install instructions on the mod builds page must be read before starting; it contains no install action of its own. Its subsections are reviewed individually below. The manual reference run executes only the Mod List steps, in order, via manual.py on a clean vanilla Steam (Windows depot, movies removed) game tree that keeps Steam's original file name spelling, under Wine on Linux; it runs nothing from this section.

Asks the user to uninstall, delete the whole game directory and reinstall so no leftover or corrupted files or old mod data remain, then to try to clear read-only flags on the game folders. The reference run satisfies this by construction: every run starts from a freshly unpacked, verified vanilla Steam game tree, and the files in the CI working tree are writable.

Asks Steam users to confirm in the game's Properties > Workshop tab that they are not subscribed to any Workshop content (for example a forgotten TSLRCM subscription). The reference run uses a game tree unpacked from the vanilla Steam Windows depot, not a Steam client install, so no Workshop content is present; TSLRCM is installed only by its own Mod List step.

Requires every archive to be fully extracted (never run TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher from inside an archive), each installer-based mod to be extracted to its own folder, the patcher to be pointed at the main game folder, loose files to go in Override with no subfolders, and warns that TSLPatcher may fail on multi-monitor setups. In the reference run each step's extract operation unpacks its archive into a fresh, separate destination under the extract root, and each patcher operation runs the mod's original TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher executable from that extracted folder under Wine, targeted at the game directory, on a single Xvfb virtual display. The linked step_ids are every Mod List step whose Installation Method line names TSLPatcher or HoloPatcher.

Warns that only one KOTOR installation may exist, because auto-detecting installers can pick the wrong one, and suggests archiving the vanilla game as a backup. The reference run has a single game tree and its patcher operations are given that game directory explicitly, so there is no second installation to be misdetected.

States that a prior build cannot be updated in place; the user must perform the zeroing step and reinstall the new build on a fresh game. The reference run always installs the current guide revision onto a fresh vanilla tree, so no prior build is present and this is satisfied.

Tells the user not to use the built-in Windows extractor and to use WinRAR or 7-Zip instead, because the native extractor fails on many of these archives. Not applicable to the reference run, which runs on Linux and extracts archives with manual.py's extract operation (7z for RAR/7z archives, Python zip/tar support otherwise) into fresh destinations.

Troubleshooting note for runtime-error crashes when cutscenes play after a load screen on some Nvidia RTX and AMD cards: disable overlays, set Nvidia low latency mode, temporarily set Fullscreen=0 and AllowWindowedMode=1 in the .ini, or as a last resort temporarily rename the movies folder. These are hardware/runtime workarounds, not install steps; the reference run does not play the game, changes no .ini setting for this, and its game tree already has movies removed.

Warns that case-sensitive Linux file systems require batch-lowercasing mod files before installer-based mods and again across the game directory afterwards, and notes Proton crash/rendering issues. The CI environment handles the case issue without lowercasing anything: manual.py matches every copy, rename and delete path against existing game entries case-insensitively (PyKotor CaseAwarePath), so a copied file overwrites an existing entry that differs only in case under its existing name instead of creating a duplicate, as on Windows, and the original patchers run under Wine, which looks up file names case-insensitively; Proton gameplay issues are not applicable because the run installs under Wine and does not play the game.

Informational list of known issues: possible leftover partially transparent textures, Visas's lightsaber possibly invisible when sparring on the Ebon Hawk, wrong camera angles in the scene of Carth on the Sojourn's bridge, and a rare load-screen crash worked around by temporarily disabling 'Frame Buffer Effects' and 'Soft Shadows'. None names a specific Mod List mod or asks for an install action; the reference run makes no change for them.

Informational: about 6.5GB of mod archives excluding movies, about 15.5GB installed including base game files excluding upscaled movies, and about 35GB with Pops Maellard's HD movies at 1920x1080. No install action; the reference run does not use it.
Introduces an optional tool that speeds up TSLPatcher installs, noting no true mod manager exists for KOTOR. It is optional and not part of the reference install; the run does not use it.

Optional registry-edit script that creates desktop symlinks to the KOTOR and KOTOR 2 directories so TSLPatcher's folder picker is quicker to use; the guide notes it does not work on Mac (or likely Linux) and changes no game files. It is optional and NOT used by this reference: patcher operations are invoked with the game directory explicitly under Wine, so no folder picker shortcut is needed.

The guide warns that the entire install could be unstable if this section is ignored: the Aspyr patch is the default version of the Steam, GoG and Mac Appstore copies, and Aspyr-patched users 'must apply the fix packages' below (3C-FD Patcher, Water Restoration, Stutter Fix) 'for this build to function properly'; legacy-version users are told to install the Aspyr patch if they want widescreen or controller support. The reference run uses the Steam Windows depot, i.e. the Aspyr version, and does NOT apply these fixes, because manual.py executes only Mod List steps. A run without them is therefore not the configuration the guide calls critical for Aspyr-version installs. Linked: step-001 '4GB Patcher', whose guide note says to perform it only if NOT on the Aspyr patch and 3C-FD has not been applied (3C-FD applies the 4GB patch itself).

Essential fix in the CRITICAL section: an executable by J that patches the game executable (all patches except experimental borderless windowed), fixing many Aspyr-patch problems and adding the 4GB/Large Address Aware patch; it requires an unedited executable without an existing 4GB patch and cannot be used on the Mac Appstore version, for which the guide advises against the 'Ultimate' upscales. It changes game files (the executable). This reference does NOT apply it, so the reference executable lacks the fixes the guide calls critical for the Aspyr (Steam) version. Linked: step-001 '4GB Patcher' (whose patch 3C-FD also applies) and the 'Ultimate' upscale steps the warning refers to.

Essential fix in the CRITICAL section: a loose-file mod by J that restores water effects removed by the Aspyr patch. It changes game files (files added to Override). This reference does NOT apply it, so the result is not the configuration the guide calls critical for the Aspyr (Steam) version.

Essential fix in the CRITICAL section: the loose-file 'Stutter Fix and Force Cage Update' by J removes water texture properties from Force cages that cause heavy visual lag, optionally with an updated cage model (forcecage_updated_1.1.0.zip contains both). It changes game files (files added to Override). This reference does NOT apply it, so the result is not the configuration the guide calls critical for the Aspyr (Steam) version.

Optional section of widescreen enhancement mods, to be installed only on the Aspyr patch, since widescreen on a legacy install is destabilizing. This reference does NOT install any mod in this section; the reference install is the Mod List only.

Optional loose-file 'Main Menu Fix for Widescreen' by DarthParametric: apply the 'for override folder' contents, and for the TSLRCM logo also the 'FOR TSLRCM' folder plus the separate 'Updated_TSLRCM_Logo_v1.8.6' download. Linked: step-002 'TSLRCM', which the TSLRCM option refers to. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional movie replacement 'K2 Cutscenes Rescaled' by Pops Maellard (about 15GB): the main file for the monitor resolution plus the matching '_mods' file when using TSLRCM or Extended Enclave, installed into the movies folder. Linked: step-002 'TSLRCM' and the 'Extended Enclave' step, which it names. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install. The run's game tree also has its movies removed, and no movie files are installed.

Optional alternative movie replacement 'KOTOR 2 Remastered Cutscenes' by naelavok (loose files, possible .bat patcher), to be used instead of Pops Maellard's set; files go in the movies folder. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install. The run's game tree also has its movies removed, and no movie files are installed.

Optional loose-file mod 'K2 Loading Screen Rescaled' by Pops Maellard, a standalone enhanced legal screen for users not installing Pops Maellard's cutscenes. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file camera tweak by DarthParametric that pulls the Workbench camera closer. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file mod by Tunalex that upscales every map, including the minimap. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.
Introductory heading for troubleshooting notes on base-game problems that are not caused by the build. The subsections are runtime workarounds reviewed below; the reference run applies none of them.

Informational: a base-game crash after character creation (or on later load screens) is avoided by disabling 'Frame Buffer Effects' in the in-game Advanced Graphics Options. This is an in-game setting, not an install step or a game file change made by this reference; the run does not play the game and makes no change for it.

Informational: an engine bug where the character is stuck after combat, tied to the framerate not syncing with the monitor refresh rate; the fix is v-sync with a 60Hz monitor setting, or setting the refresh rate in the game's .ini to the monitor's rate. These are display or user configuration settings; this reference does not change the .ini or apply either option.

Informational: if the swoop bike floats above the track, temporarily launch the game in Windows XP SP3 compatibility mode for the race, then turn it off. This is a launch-time compatibility setting, not a game file change; it is not applicable to the reference run, which does not launch or play the game.

Informational: explains memory-leak-related dialogue skipping, mostly caused by the Aspyr patch and largely resolved by the 3C-FD patcher, as distinct from the Aspyr input-delay 'dialogue floatiness' that remains. No install action of its own; note that this reference does not apply the 3C-FD patcher (see the CRITICAL section review), so the mitigation described here is not present in the reference install.
